observations.finding: The qualified root-water-uptake process request carries potential_transpiration. Per rooted node it computes qpotential as a root-fraction increment times potential_transpiration, sets root_extraction_sink(node)=qpotential*drought_reduction_factor, and defines actual_uptake_total=sum(root_extraction_sink).

On the explicit provider route, root_sink_term(node) is the provider root_extraction_sink(node) and is added directly to the compartment residual alongside vertical/source/sink flux terms. It is not multiplied by layer thickness at this boundary.

The current runtime root-uptake binding is committed-state oriented: it accepts kernel_committed_state_t and builds the hydraulic view from committed state. It therefore is not by itself a rejected-trial-safe owner of process accumulation during a candidate physical trial.
The current process hydraulic-view builder accepts kernel_committed_state_t only. No parallel candidate/trial-state hydraulic-view builder is present on the pinned canonical source tree.

kernel_candidate_state_t provides snapshot access to candidate physical state, so a future trial-view seam is technically possible without changing F-KT commit authority. This does not itself define the correct root-uptake temporal semantics.

The physical interval forcing already contains root_extraction_sink and the backend binds this sink before the Richards trial is advanced. The current serialized solver route therefore consumes a preformed root sink during the trial rather than recomputing the Feddes uptake process inside Newton iterations.
The root-sink provider returns the supplied root_extraction_sink vector unchanged; it does not own crop potential transpiration or accepted-window provenance.
The MultiSWAP runtime owns checkpoint/trial/commit flow and receives a fully formed forcing_registry, but its request does not carry the crop-root process request or potential_transpiration.

resolved_dimensional_mapping.reason: The root-uptake process constructs each layer value as a fraction of potential_transpiration and sums these values to actual_uptake_total; HeadCalc consumes each provider value directly as a flux contribution in the water-balance residual.
